_comment: The computer rival. It plays by the player's rules: it only knows what its own sensors have seen, plus what anyone can see on the map (planets, who holds them, claims in progress). It thinks every thinkHours (Easy also skips a step now and then (slipChance), wants extraRatio more strength, never gathers for a strike, never chains claims and only defends its own planets): picks a goal, gives each fleet a job, and pulls back from fights it expects to lose. Power is a rough fighting value per ship (its cost, less for damage and empty missile racks); unseen enemy ships are guessed from what the enemy earns. attackRatio is how much stronger it wants to be before attacking; each game rolls a value between min and max (moved by the personality), and it drifts by up to nerveDrift each day within nerveRange of that roll. Claim groups that take a planet move on to another within chainClaimAu; at most claimGroups claim at once. When the home fleet is too small to strike but would be big enough with the claim groups back, it calls them home and starts no claims for gatherDays. A strike flies at the fastest speed that still arrives with strikeSuppliesLeft of its supplies. Of the enemy power it has not seen elsewhere, it assumes homeShareSeen guards the enemy shipyard when it has fresh eyes there, else homeShareUnseen. Distances are in AU.
_campaignComment: Campaign: from campaignAfterDays after its first probe, when the home fleet (less its guard share, at least campaignMinShips ships) could take on what guards an enemy colony (seen nearby, plus gunValue per rail battery, plus campaignRelief of the enemy power it has not seen lately, which might come to help) at fightRatio odds, it sends that fleet to blockade and take the colony, no more than campaignMaxDays away. It breaks an enemy claim on its own planet at defendOwnRatio odds (worse odds than it wants elsewhere) and hunts enemy fleets near its planets at fightRatio x huntOdds.
_mirrorComment: Its guess of the enemy's fighting power is the larger of what it has seen and the smaller of: what the enemy could have built from its Industry (enemyBuildShare), and mirrorShare times its own fighting power scaled by how their holdings compare (ships are limited by materials, not Industry).
_restlessComment: After restlessAfterDays without a battle a side grows restless: over the next restlessDays the odds it wants for a campaign fall by up to restlessMax (scaled by 0.5 + aggression), so two big fleets don't sit at home for ever.
_personalitiesComment: Each game rolls a personality (as likely as its weight, default 1) plus small leanings. profile: six axes, 0 to 1. aggression: how soon and at what odds the main fleet goes on a campaign (odds wanted 1.25 - 0.5 x aggression). expansion: settle orders at a time (1 + 2 x expansion). defence: at 0.7 or more, a rail battery and a point defence grid on each colony with people. risk: how much stronger nearby enemies must be before a fleet on a job turns back (dangerRatio x (0.8 + 0.4 x risk)). raiding: at 0.5 or more it lies in wait on enemy supply lanes with small fast groups (one party, two from 0.7, three from 0.9), hunts with small groups from 0.7, and goes further for a convoy (0.5 + raiding AU). research: Industry it lets research spend before the next ship. pullBack: its usual preset (cautious, standard, fightOn; now and then another, to compare). fireAt: weakest, largest, split, engines, flagship (under light lag; else nearest), or roll (a different rule each battle). missiles: close, mid or far. extraFreighters and buildEveryDays (days between non-urgent planet buildings): the trader's richer economy. The opportunist re-picks a focus every focusDays (take, raid, hunt or expand: where the enemy looks weakest) and raises that axis.
_automationComment: The player's automation areas (see Stewards): starting level of each (auto, advise, manual) and how the defaults learn from the player's changes and from how auto actions turn out.
